sum: The classic loop up the Marsyangdi valley to Manang, over the Thorong La at 5,416 m and down to Muktinath and Jomsom, planned around the roads that now flank it.
reach: By tourist bus (7–9 hours) or by air (about 25 minutes).

guide.note: Since April 2023 the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers in conservation areas to walk with a licensed guide, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route a guide earns the fee by holding you to the acclimatization schedule, finding the side trails that avoid the road, and making the call on whether to start for the pass when the weather is doubtful.

access: Besisahar is the road gateway, six to seven hours by bus from Kathmandu or four to five from Pokhara. Jeeps continue up the Marsyangdi on a rough road to Dharapani, Chame and Manang. The trek ends at Jomsom, which has morning flights and a long road to Pokhara.

photo.a: The flat-roofed houses of Manang spread across a dry valley floor below eroded cliffs and the snow-covered slopes of Annapurna III and Gangapurna.
photo.c: Manang below Annapurna III and Gangapurna

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus and shared jeep at both ends of the trek

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

transportText: Bus from Kathmandu to Besisahar and a jeep seat up the valley; at the end a flight or a jeep seat from Jomsom to Pokhara, and the tourist bus back to Kathmandu
tips: Carry cash for the whole trek. The machines in Chame and Jomsom cannot be relied on, and there is nothing dependable in between.
Look for the red-and-white and blue-and-white paint marks of the NATT trails wherever the route meets the road.
Take the upper trail from Upper Pisang even if you are tired. The lower route follows the road and misses the best views.
For the pass carry two litres of water in bottles that will not freeze, snacks, sunglasses and, after any snowfall, microspikes.
Leave Thorong Phedi no later than five. Wind on the pass strengthens from about ten.

days.t: Drive to Besisahar, jeep to Dharapani
days.note: Bus to Besisahar, four to five hours from Pokhara or six to seven from Kathmandu, then three to four hours by shared jeep up the Marsyangdi gorge. The road is rough and narrow. Permits are checked at Dharapani, where the Manaslu trail comes in.

Follow the road and its footpath shortcuts through Bagarchhap to Danakyu, then take the steep forest trail up to Timang, which leaves the road behind and looks back at Manaslu. An easier stretch through Thanchok and Koto leads to Chame, with Annapurna II and Lamjung Himal ahead.

Pine forest and apple orchards to Bhratang, then the valley bends beneath the great curved slab of Paungda Danda. After Dhikur Pokhari leave the road, cross the river and climb to Upper Pisang. You are now above 3,000 m, so slow down and keep the afternoon easy.

days.t: Upper Pisang to Manang by the high route
days.note: The best day on the eastern side. A long set of switchbacks climbs about 400 m to Ghyaru, then a balcony trail runs to Ngawal with Annapurna II, III, IV and Gangapurna across the valley. Descend to the valley floor and walk on through Braga to Manang. Going high and sleeping lower helps you acclimatize.

Do not skip this, and take a second day if you arrived by jeep or still have a headache. Climb to Praken Gompa above the village, or to the Chongkor viewpoint over Gangapurna Lake, come down for lunch, and go to the aid post's afternoon talk on altitude if it is running.

A short stage on purpose. The trail climbs out of the Marsyangdi valley past Tanki Manang and Gunsang into the side valley that leads to the pass, through juniper scrub and yak pasture. Arrive by lunch, then walk a little higher in the afternoon and come back down.

An hour to Ledar, then down to a bridge and up to a narrow path across loose slopes where stones fall; cross without stopping. You reach Phedi by lunch. Walk part of the way toward High Camp in the afternoon, eat early and pack for a pre-dawn start.

days.t: Over the Thorong La to Muktinath
days.note: Leave between four and five. A steep hour of zigzags reaches High Camp, then the trail climbs more gently over moraine, past several false summits, to the prayer flags on the pass. The descent is 1,650 m of loose trail and hard on the knees; tea shops begin at Chabarbu, about an hour above Muktinath.

Visit the temple early, then descend through Jharkot and Khinga to the mud-walled lanes of Kagbeni for lunch. The last three hours follow the Kali Gandaki riverbed and road into a strong afternoon headwind. Many people take a jeep from Muktinath or Kagbeni instead; the quieter footpath goes by Lubra.

Flights leave soon after dawn and stop once the valley wind rises, so cancellations are common. The alternative is eight to ten hours by bus or jeep down the Kali Gandaki through Tatopani and Beni. Keep a spare day before any onward travel.
